name: moving-boundary
title: Moving boundary: diffusion on a deforming (ALE) domain
question:
Does a real dolfinx diffusion solve, re-assembled and re-solved every
substep on a mesh whose geometry is mutated in place according to a
prescribed moving-boundary law (prescribed ALE mesh motion), stay
numerically well-behaved -- boundary tracking the prescribed law, domain
measure scaling correctly with the deformation amplitude, field staying
finite -- when wrapped as a process-bigraph Process?
hypothesis:
`MovingBoundaryProcess` should reproduce the prescribed top-boundary law
`y_top(t)` to near machine precision (the mesh deformation is an exact
uniform vertical stretch, not an approximation), the FEM-assembled domain
area should scale linearly with the oscillation amplitude (a larger
amplitude produces a proportionally larger swing in domain measure away
from the base area), and the diffusion field solved on the deforming mesh
should remain finite and bounded throughout, since no term in the
backward-Euler diffusion assembly can blow up under a smooth, bounded
mesh deformation.
objective:
Run the `moving_boundary` composite (a single `MovingBoundaryProcess` --
real dolfinx diffusion re-solved on a prescribed-ALE deforming mesh) and
verify (a) `boundary_position` tracks the prescribed oscillation law to
near machine precision, (b) `domain_measure`'s swing away from the base
area scales with the oscillation amplitude across an amplitude sweep, and
(c) the diffusion field stays finite and bounded across the run.
description:
Wraps a single `MovingBoundaryProcess` in the `moving_boundary` composite
generator. Each tick, the process advances the mesh motion and diffusion
field by `dt`-sized substeps: (1) evaluate the prescribed boundary law
`y_top(t)` (`mode="oscillate"`: `1 + amplitude*sin(omega*t)`;
`mode="grow"`: `1 + amplitude*t`), (2) mutate `domain.geometry.x` in
place -- a uniform vertical stretch of the reference (t=0) unit-square
y-coordinates, mapping the fixed bottom boundary to y=0 and the moving
top boundary to y=y_top(t) -- and (3) re-assemble and re-solve a
backward-Euler diffusion step with a fresh `dolfinx.fem.petsc.LinearProblem`
on that deformed geometry. This is the PRESCRIBED-mesh-motion ALE
fallback explicitly sanctioned for this showcase (real dolfinx geometry
mutation + a genuine re-solve every substep on the true deformed cells --
not a mock, not a cosmetic coordinate transform after the fact). Because
only the domain's height changes (width stays 1), the FEM-assembled
`domain_measure` (`integral(1) dx` over the current mesh) should equal
`boundary_position` to near machine precision -- a strong,
non-tautological cross-check that the mesh geometry really was mutated.

This is an ADVANCED, showcase-tier study: it is the investigation's only
deforming-domain demo, and the first process whose mesh itself (not just
its solution field) is time-varying state.

expected_behavior.name: boundary-follows-prescribed-law
expected_behavior.en: boundary_position at the end of the baseline run matches the analytic oscillation law 1 + amplitude*sin(omega*t) to within 1e-4.
expected_behavior.rationale: The mesh deformation is an exact uniform vertical stretch of the reference y-coordinates by y_top(t), so the mesh's actual top-boundary coordinate should track the prescribed law to near machine precision, not merely approximately -- confirming the ALE mesh motion is a real geometry mutation driven by the prescribed law, not an independent or drifting quantity.

expected_behavior.name: domain-measure-scales-with-amplitude
expected_behavior.en: The domain_measure swing (max deviation from the base area 1.0) for the amplitude=0.5 variant is at least 3x that of the amplitude=0.1 variant.
expected_behavior.rationale: domain_measure = 1 * y_top(t) exactly (unit-width domain), so its deviation from the base area 1.0 should scale linearly with the oscillation amplitude; a 5x amplitude ratio (0.5 vs 0.1) should produce a clearly separated swing ratio, well above solver/sampling noise.

expected_behavior.name: field-stays-finite
expected_behavior.en: The diffusion field's maximum absolute value stays below 5.0 throughout the baseline run (no blow-up on the deforming mesh).
expected_behavior.rationale: Backward-Euler diffusion is unconditionally stable for any fixed mesh; re-solving it every substep on a smoothly, boundedly deforming mesh should not introduce a blow-up mechanism -- this test locks that the prescribed-ALE re-solve stays numerically well-behaved across the run.

behavior_tests.name: boundary-follows-prescribed-law
behavior_tests.description:
abs(boundary_position(T) - (1 + amplitude*sin(omega*T))) for the
baseline run must be below 1e-4 at the final recorded time T.

provenance.note: The mesh motion is deform_mesh()'s exact uniform stretch by y_top(t); the only departure from exact equality is floating-point roundoff (observed ~1e-15 during development), so 1e-4 leaves enormous headroom while still catching a genuinely broken mesh motion (e.g. a stale/undeformed mesh).

behavior_tests.name: domain-measure-scales-with-amplitude
behavior_tests.description:
max(|domain_measure - 1.0|) over the amplitude=0.5 variant's run must
be at least 3x the same quantity for the amplitude=0.1 variant, over
the same duration/wiring.

provenance.note: domain_measure = y_top(t) exactly, so the analytic swing ratio for a 5x amplitude ratio is exactly 5.0; 3.0 leaves headroom for transient/sampling effects (peak not landing exactly at the same sampled tick in both runs) while still catching a broken or amplitude-insensitive mesh motion.

behavior_tests.name: field-stays-finite
behavior_tests.description:
max(|field|) across every recorded frame of the baseline run must stay
below 5.0 -- no blow-up from re-solving on the deforming mesh.

provenance.note: Backward-Euler diffusion of a bounded gaussian-bump initial condition (peak amplitude 1.0) with no source term cannot exceed its initial peak in the continuous limit; 5.0 leaves generous headroom for discretization overshoot on the deforming mesh while still catching a genuine numerical blow-up.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
No further studies in this investigation currently depend on
moving-boundary; it is the investigation's deforming-domain showcase,
built on top of navier-stokes (the investigation's other advanced,
showcase-tier study) rather than directly on the scalar
diffusion/reaction studies.
